blocks.text: For general information about modals, see Unit 19.

rows.example: **must / mustn't** · **have to** · **need to** — All visitors **must** turn off their mobile phones. You **have to / need to** press 'send'.
**don't have to / don't need to / needn't** — You **don't have to / don't need to / needn't** pay to send an e-mail.
**had to** — Yesterday, Sam **had to** buy more stamps.
**didn't have to / didn't need to** — I learnt a little Italian, but everyone spoke English, so I **didn't have to / didn't need to** use it.

blocks.intro: In spoken English, **have to** is more common than **must**. **Must** is often used in written notices and instructions.
items: **We have to** pay the phone bill today, Rita said.
Passengers **must** turn off all mobile phones.

blocks.text: **Mustn't** and **don't have to** do not mean the same.
blocks.note: You **mustn't** do that! (= Don't do that!) · You **don't have to** do that. (= You can do that if you want to, but it's not necessary.)

rows.example: **must / can't / couldn't** — The phone is ringing — it **must** be Simon. This letter **can't / couldn't** be from Japan because it's got a French stamp.
**should / ought to** — We **ought to / should** hear from Cheryl this weekend.
**could / may / might** — I'm not sure what language it is — it **could / may / might** be Polish.

blocks.intro: We often use **must**, **can't** and **couldn't** for probability when we have some evidence for our opinion.
items: I just rang Paul, but there's no answer. He **must** be out.

blocks.text: To talk about possibility and probability about the past, we use a modal and the perfect infinitive. See Unit 22.

exercises.title: A · Same meaning?
exercises.instruction: Choose the sentence which means the same as the first sentence.

items.prompt: We have to pay the electricity bill before Friday.
options: We can pay it if we want to.

items.prompt: You don't need to buy me a birthday present.
options: You must buy me a birthday present.
It's not necessary to buy me a birthday present.
You mustn't buy me a birthday present.
acceptedAnswers: It's not necessary to buy me a birthday present.

items.prompt: I have to do some work on my project this evening.
options: I haven't got time to do the work.
I need to do the work.
acceptedAnswers: I need to do the work.

items.prompt: Lenny didn't have to see the head teacher after all.
options: It wasn't necessary for Lenny to see the head teacher.
Lenny went to see the head teacher.
Lenny is waiting to see the head teacher.
acceptedAnswers: It wasn't necessary for Lenny to see the head teacher.

items.prompt: Students mustn't run in school buildings.
options: They can run if they want to.

items.prompt: All passengers must fasten their seatbelts.
options: They have to fasten their seatbelts now.
They don't have to fasten their seatbelts.
acceptedAnswers: They have to fasten their seatbelts now.

items.prompt: Mr Reed had to go to the police station to answer some questions.
options: Mr Reed was able to go to the police station.
Mr Reed forgot to go to the police station.
Mr Reed was obliged to go to the police station.
acceptedAnswers: Mr Reed was obliged to go to the police station.

items.prompt: It's kind of you to offer to help, but you really don't need to.
options: I don't want you to help me.
You won't be able to help me.

exercises.title: B · Circle the correct phrase
exercises.instruction: Select the form that fits the meaning.

items.prompt: 'Smoking isn't allowed in the airport.' You ___ smoke in the airport.
'It's not necessary to come to the train station to meet me.' You ___ meet her at the train station.
'We were forced to wait for over two hours in the rain!' They ___ wait for over two hours in the rain.
'The instructions tell you to write in pencil.' You ___ write in pencil.
'You can contact us by either phone or e-mail.' You ___ phone them.
'In my country, you can carry your passport with you if you want, but it's not necessary.' In her country, you ___ carry your passport with you.
'My grandfather was made to start work when he was just fourteen years old.' He ___ start work when he was just fourteen years old.
'It's not necessary to book a hotel; you can stay in our spare room.' You ___ stay in a hotel.

exercises.title: C · have to
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct form of have to. You may need a negative form.

items.prompt: Jade can't come out tonight. She ___ look after her little brother.
I didn't have enough money, so I ___ borrow some from Yuri.
It's raining really hard, but luckily we ___ go out this evening.
To start the laptop you ___ press the power button.
Robbie worked last weekend, but I ___ .
___ go to piano lessons when you were younger? (you / have to)

exercises.title: D · How certain?
exercises.instruction: Match each sentence with the explanation.

items.prompt: 'Someone is at the door. It must be Mrs Johnson from next door.'
'Lena might not know where the cinema is.'
'Dad should know what the capital of New Zealand is.'
'Greg can't be in the final! He's a terrible player!'
'The dog is wet. It must be raining outside.'
'We may go to the Canary Islands for Easter.'
'Ken must like that film. He's seen it six times!'
'Barry ought to be able to cook Chinese food. He lived there for two years.'

exercises.title: E · Rewrite with the modal
exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentences using the words given.

items.prompt: You're expecting David to ring. The phone rings. **must**
Anna is a better runner than Rula. You think Anna will probably win the race tomorrow. **should**
acceptedAnswers: Anna should win the race tomorrow.
Anna should win the race tomorrow

items.prompt: A letter arrives. It's possible that it's from your cousin, Janice. **could**
acceptedAnswers: It could be from my cousin Janice.
It could be from my cousin, Janice.

items.prompt: There's a knock at the door. Your mum says it might be Colin, but you know Colin is on holiday. **can't**
acceptedAnswers: It can't be Colin because he's on holiday.
It can't be Colin because he's on holiday

items.prompt: You see someone wearing a costume. You think there's a strong probability that she's going to a fancy-dress party. **must**
acceptedAnswers: She must be going to a fancy-dress party.
She must be going to a fancy-dress party
She must be going to a fancy dress party.
She must be going to a fancy dress party

acceptedAnswers: It might be in the living room.
It might be in the living room

acceptedAnswers: She should be there in half an hour.
She should be there in half an hour
Harriet should be there in half an hour.
Harriet should be there in half an hour

acceptedAnswers: He could be in trouble at school.
